papers.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Added to Statin Therapy and Cardiovascular Outcomes in ASCVD A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study
papers.abstract: Objective: To evaluate whether GLP-1 RA use added to statins is associated with lower all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction (MI), and ischemic stroke versus statin monotherapy in ASCVD patients with body mass index (BMI) 30 kg/m2. Approach and Results:Using the TriNetX Research Network (108 U.S. healthcare organizations), we identified ASCVD patients with BMI 30 kg/m2 on statins initiating a GLP-1 RA (n=166,278) versus statin-only controls (n=920,176). Propensity score matching on 34 covariates yielded 119,911 matched pairs followed 3 years. Prespecified analyses included a BMI 35 subgroup (62,385 pairs), four washout sensitivity analyses (30-120 days), and a familial hypercholesterolemia exclusion analysis (161,312 matched pairs). Results. GLP-1 RA use was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality (4.0% vs. 7.5%; HR 0.479; 95% CI: 0.463-0.496; p<0.001), MI (HR 0.762; 95% CI: 0.737-0.788; p<0.001), and ischemic stroke (HR 0.671; 95% CI: 0.588-0.766; p<0.001). Benefits were consistent across the BMI 35 subgroup and all washout analyses. GLP-1 RA users were more likely to achieve LDL <55 mg/dL by risk analysis (17.1% vs. 15.3%; RR 1.118; p<0.001); the Kaplan-Meier analysis was non-significant (HR 1.007; p=0.538). Mortality benefit was preserved in the FH exclusion analysis. Conclusion: ASCVD patients with obesity on statins, GLP-1 RA use was associated with substantially lower mortality, MI, and stroke, suggesting GLP-1 RAs may serve as cardioprotective adjuncts to statin therapy in this population.

papers.title: Late-Stage Concentration of Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Burden in US Adults: Disability-Adjusted Life Years Across AHA Stages, 2005 to 2023
papers.abstract: Background: Cardiovascular prevention is increasingly prioritised using burden estimates, yet disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) reward late-stage treatment by construction. Whether that bias is large for cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, and where the population is accumulating relative to where the burden sits, is unknown. Methods: We pooled nine National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cycles (2005-2023) and assigned CKM stages 0-4 from measured blood pressure, adiposity, glycaemia, lipids, kidney function, urine albumin, self-reported cardiovascular disease, and 10-year PREVENT risk. Years lived with disability used GBD disability weights. Years of life lost combined national death counts, stage-specific mortality from linked mortality files (1999-2018), and period life tables. A second aim attributed burden to smoking and physical inactivity, two exposures outside the CKM definition. Results: In 2021-2023, 13.8% of adults were stage 0, 21.3% stage 1, 49.1% stage 2, 6.5% stage 3, and 9.3% stage 4. CKM accounted for 20.0 million DALYs annually (7,881 age-standardised per 100,000), of which 4.1 million were YLD and 15.9 million attributable YLL. Stages 3-4, 15.8% of adults, generated 76% of attributable YLL; stage 4 alone generated 65% of YLD and 49% of attributable YLL. Adjusted mortality rose from stage 2 (hazard ratio 1.39) through stage 4 (3.22), while stage 1 did not differ from stage 0 (0.99; 95% CI, 0.78-1.25). Between 2006 and 2016, stage 0 prevalence fell 2.3% per year and stage 1 rose 3.1% per year. Smoking and physical inactivity accounted for 30.5% of burden (95% CI, 25.7-35.1). Conclusions: CKM burden is concentrated in stages 3-4, where excess mortality begins, while the population has been shifting into stage 1, where mortality is normal. DALY-based prioritisation will therefore systematically underfund the stage in which the next generation of patients is being created.

papers.title: Routine CBC-Derived Markers of Systemic Inflammation Are Associated With Growth of the Dilated Ascending Aorta During CT Surveillance
papers.abstract: Background: Ascending aortic surveillance relies on diameter thresholds, yet most dissections occur below them. Inflammation drives aortic wall remodeling independent of diameter. Inflammation drives aortic wall remodeling independent of diameter. Inflammatory indices derived from routine blood counts, such as neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), red cell distribution width (RDW), and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) have been show to predict adverse cardiovascular outcomes, but their association with ascending aortic growth is unclear. Methods and Results: We retrospectively studied adults with 2 computed tomography (CT) scans of the native ascending aorta 6 months apart at a single center (2000-2023), excluding those with aortitis or no complete blood count during follow-up. Markers were summarized as 95th percentile values per patient and per scan interval. Growth was defined as a 2-mm increase in mid-ascending aortic diameter. Patient-level logistic regression and interval-level generalized estimating equation models were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, baseline diameter, systolic blood pressure, diabetes, and heritable thoracic aortic disease. Among 3,262 patients, data were available in 1,882 for RDW, 1,471 for NLR, and 1,468 for SII; 192 (10.2%) met criteria for growth. Only RDW was independently associated with growth in the overall cohort (patient level: odds ratio [OR] 1.071, 95% CI 1.002-1.144, p=0.043; interval level: OR 1.075, 95% CI 1.012-1.141, p=0.019); NLR (p=0.080) and SII (p=0.164) were not. Among patients with guideline-defined ascending aortic dilation (40 mm), all three markers were associated with interval growth (RDW OR 1.14, NLR OR 1.05, SII OR 1.01 per 100 units; all p 0.014), whereas none were among aortas <40 mm; effect modification was significant for NLR (p=0.01). Conclusions: RDW was modestly associated with ascending aortic growth overall, and all three markers were associated with interval growth in patients with guideline-defined aortic dilation, suggesting that systemic inflammation may contribute to progression of aortic dilation. Prospective studies with more specific inflammatory markers are needed.

papers.title: Biomarker-Informed Phenotyping of the Heart Failure Continuum: A Population-Based Evaluation of the Second Universal Definition of Heart Failure
papers.abstract: Objective: To develop and evaluate a biomarker-informed, computable phenotype of the heart failure (HF) continuum, aligned with 2026 AHA/ACC/ESC/WHF Expert Consensus, using NHANES and linked mortality data, and to determine whether this phenotype identifies subgroups with distinct mortality risks. Methods: We analyzed 11,477 U.S. adults aged [≥]20 years from the 1999-2004 NHANES cycles who participated in the surplus-sera biomarker substudy and were linked to National Death Index follow-up. Participants were classified into four phenotypes according to the 2026 Universal Definition of Heart Failure: no apparent risk, Stage A (at risk), Stage B (elevated NT-proBNP without self-reported HF), and Stage C (self-reported HF). Survey-weighted Kaplan-Meier curves and nested, multiply imputed Cox proportional hazards models, with sequential adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic, and cardiometabolic covariates, were used to estimate associations with mortality. Pairwise phenotype comparisons, standardized adjusted survival estimates, and restricted mean survival times were also calculated. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated by comparing discrimination and reclassification metrics between the full phenotype and a conventional three-level model that excluded NT-proBNP. Results: Weighted prevalences were 16.9%, 70.0%, 10.7%, and 2.4% for no apparent risk, Stage A, Stage B, and Stage C, respectively. In fully adjusted models, the hazard ratios (HRs) relative to no apparent risk were 1.58 (95% CI, 1.08-2.30), 2.88 (95% CI, 2.00-4.16), and 2.56 (95% CI, 1.61-4.09), respectively. Stage B was associated with significantly higher mortality risk than Stage A (HR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.62-2.07), whereas the difference between Stage C and Stage B was not statistically significant (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.71-1.11). The association for Stage B attenuated less across sequentially adjusted models than that for Stage C. Adjusted 10-year mortality risks were 15.2% for Stage B and 14.2% for Stage C. Incorporating Stage B into the conventional model yielded only marginal improvements in discrimination ({Delta}C-statistic, 0.002; 95% CI, 0.001-0.002). Conclusion: A biomarker-informed phenotype of the HF continuum can be operationalized using national survey data and identifies a pre-HF subgroup with an adjusted mortality risk not significantly different from that of individuals with overt HF, despite only marginal gains in prognostic discrimination.

papers.title: Hypoxic Burden Predicts Symptomatic but Not Sleep Architecture Response to CPAP Therapy in Obstructive Sleep Apnea
papers.abstract: The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) remains the standard metric for assessing obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity, although it does not fully capture the physiological consequences of respiratory events. Hypoxic burden (HB), which integrates the frequency, depth, and duration of oxygen desaturations, has been proposed as a more comprehensive measure of OSA-related hypoxic stress. This study compared the prognostic value of HB and AHI for subjective and objective treatment outcomes in patients undergoing continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy. Data from 412 patients with OSA who underwent diagnostic and CPAP-treated polysomnography were analyzed, including 52 patients with available follow-up questionnaires. HB was calculated using a validated event-based algorithm. Multivariable regression models were used to predict patient-reported outcomes and changes in sleep architecture, adjusted for age, sex and body mass index. HB consistently demonstrated stronger associations with symptomatic outcomes than AHI. Models including HB showed improved model fit and explained variance. HB remained independently associated with lower follow-up fatigue and better sleep quality after adjustment for AHI. In contrast, AHI was the dominant predictor of objective sleep architecture improvements, including increases in N3 sleep, reductions in N1 sleep, and reductions in arousal index. HB provided additional independent information only for changes in arousal burden. These findings suggest that HB and AHI capture complementary dimensions of OSA severity. While AHI primarily reflects sleep fragmentation and physiological response to CPAP, HB appears more closely related to subjective treatment benefit. Incorporating HB alongside AHI may improve clinical phenotyping and prediction of treatment response in OSA.

papers.title: Digital Twin-Based Risk Stratification Integrating Aortic Shape and Wall Mechanics in Acute Uncomplicated Type B Aortic Dissection
papers.abstract: Objective This study evaluated whether patient-specific digital twins integrating 3D aortic anatomy and structural wall stress could identify patients with acute uncomplicated type B aortic dissection (AUTBAD) at high risk for adverse aortic events. Methods We analyzed CTAs from 50 patients extracted from a 400 AUTBAD patient database treated with optimal medical therapy from 1999-2025. Digital twin models were constructed, and statistical shape modeling and reduced-order fluid-structure interaction analysis were performed. Anatomic shape and biomechanical stress data were integrated into models predicting freedom from aortic events, defined as intervention or aortic-related death, using leave-one-out cross-validation. A cross-validated risk score was generated for each patient, with higher scores indicating higher event risk. Results At diagnosis, the median descending aortic diameter was 40.61 mm. During follow-up, 35 patients experienced an aortic event: 28 interventions (56%) and 7 aortic-related deaths (14%). Stratification by descending aortic diameter above or below 40.61 mm yielded higher- versus lower-risk aortic event-free survival of 72.0% versus 84.0% at 1 year and 27.8% versus 56.7% at 6 years (p=0.035; C-index=0.590). In the cross-validated multidimensional model combining morphology and structural stress, higher- versus lower-risk event-free survival was 60.0% versus 96.0% at 1 year and 12.5% versus 68.9% at 6 years (p<0.001; C-index=0.792). Conclusions Digital twin modeling integrating morphology and wall stress provided greater risk separation than univariable predictors in AUTBAD patients. With independent validation, patient-specific AUTBAD risk stratification using geometric and biomechanical data may ultimately contribute to identification of high-risk patients who may benefit from early endovascular repair.

papers.title: Cumulative Multidomain Vulnerability and Early Mortality After Heart Transplantation: Development and Temporal Evaluation of the RIGHT-HTx Framework
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Risk models from high-income transplant programmes may not generalise to resource-constrained settings with different recipient acuity, donor characteristics and access to mechanical circulatory support. We developed RIGHT-HTx, a parsimonious framework integrating clinical and physiological vulnerabilities, and evaluated its prognostic performance in a subsequent same-centre cohort. METHODS This retrospective single-centre study included 436 consecutive adult heart transplant recipients (2012-2026). Of 357 development recipients, 341 (95.5%) were score-evaluable. RIGHT-HTx incorporated three vulnerability domains: clinical acuity (INTERMACS 1-2), graded renal dysfunction (eGFR 30-59 or 12 mmHg combined with donor-to-recipient weight ratio <1.0). A seven-point Cox-derived score underwent internal validation using 1,000 bootstrap resamples and was applied unchanged to 79 subsequent recipients. Low-, intermediate- and high-risk categories represented zero, one and 2 affected domains, respectively. RESULTS Among development recipients, 75/341 (22.0%) died within one year. Mortality increased across low-, intermediate- and high-risk categories (8.1%, 20.3% and 55.6%; log-rank P<0.001). Elevated TPG was not significantly associated with mortality individually, whereas its combination with donor undersizing was independently associated with mortality (adjusted HR 2.87, 95% CI 1.53-5.40; P=0.001). The full model improved discrimination beyond renal dysfunction alone (optimism-corrected C-index 0.067), and the simplified score achieved an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.732. The temporal cohort more often had 1 affected domain (75.9% versus 60.4%; P=0.010). Discrimination was comparable (C-index 0.738, 95% CI 0.643-0.833), although observed Kaplan-Meier one-year mortality exceeded original predictions (35.4% versus 25.4%; calibration slope 0.929). In pooled analyses (n=420), mortality increased from 8.4% (13/154) with no affected domain to 57.3% (47/82) with two or more. CONCLUSIONS RIGHT-HTx identifies cumulative multidomain vulnerability associated with early mortality after heart transplantation. Temporal discrimination was comparable, but absolute-risk calibration differed. The framework may support risk recognition and mitigation, not transplant eligibility or allocation; independent multicentre validation is required before clinical implementation.

papers.title: Early Valve Replacement vs Surveillance in Moderate Aortic Stenosis: Meta-Analysis of Randomized and Observational Evidence
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Moderate aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with excess mortality, and 2 randomized trials have tested early transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). OBJECTIVES: The authors sought to estimate the effects of early TAVR vs clinical surveillance and to compare randomized with observational estimates. METHODS: Six databases and registries were searched through November 3, 2026. Adjusted observational studies were synthesized separately from trials. Certainty was rated with GRADE. RESULTS: Two trials (922 patients; TAVR UNLOAD, n = 178, HF with reduced ejection fraction; PROGRESS, n = 744, 96.4% symptomatic) and 7 cohorts were included. Early TAVR did not detectably change death over approximately 2 years (HR: 1.05; 95% CI: 0.74-1.49; low certainty), with one-fifth of the deaths needed to detect a 20% reduction. Heart failure (HF) hospitalization was lower (RR: 0.53; 95% CI: 0.36-0.77; low certainty), or 70 fewer patients per 1,000 at 2 years. New pacemakers were more frequent (PROGRESS: 17.3% vs 9.3%; moderate certainty). About half of surveillance patients underwent valve replacement within 2 years. Observational cohorts estimated a 48% mortality reduction (HR: 0.52; 95% CI: 0.43-0.64; very low certainty), which differed from the randomized estimate (ratio of HRs: 2.01; 95% CI: 1.37-2.95). CONCLUSIONS: In older, predominantly symptomatic patients with moderate AS, early TAVR may make little or no difference to 2-year mortality and may reduce HF hospitalization, at the cost of more pacemakers. Because about half of patients under surveillance receive a valve within 2 years, the decision largely concerns timing. Observational survival estimates should not guide practice.

papers.title: Associations of Pathogenic Sequence Variants and Copy Number Variants with Cardiovascular and Major Clinical Outcomes in Adults with Congenital Heart Disease
papers.abstract: Background: Genetic abnormalities contribute to the phenotypic heterogeneity of congenital heart disease, yet their prognostic significance in adults with congenital heart disease remains incompletely understood. We examined the associations of pathogenic sequence variants and copy number variants (CNVs) with cardiovascular and major clinical outcomes in ACHD. Methods: In this prospective observational cohort study, 1,000 adults with structurally confirmed CHD were recruited from a tertiary care center in Noida, India, between January 2022 and January 2026 and followed through August 2026. Participants underwent exome sequencing and chromosomal microarray analysis and were classified into four mutually exclusive groups: reference, sequence-variant-only, CNV-only, and dual-positive. The primary outcome was time to first occurrence of a composite of cardiovascular death, unplanned heart failure hospitalization, resuscitated cardiac arrest, sustained ventricular tachyarrhythmia, heart transplantation, or durable mechanical circulatory support. Associations were evaluated using multivariable Cox regression. Results: Of 1,000 participants, 800 comprised the reference group, 120 had sequence variants only, 60 had CNVs only, and 20 had both sequence variants and CNVs. Over a median follow-up of 4.2 years, the primary outcome occurred in 12.0%, 20.0%, 25.0%, and 30.0% of participants, respectively. In fully adjusted analyses, the sequence-variant-only group had a higher risk of the primary outcome versus the reference group (hazard ratio [HR], 1.65; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.01?2.69; p=0.0455). The CNV-only group had an HR of 1.92 (95% CI, 1.04?3.52; p=0.0360). Neither association remained significant after Holm adjustment (adjusted p=0.072 for both). The dual-positive group had an HR of 2.12 (95% CI, 0.83?5.42; p=0.1182). Extracardiac congenital anomalies and neurological disorders were more prevalent among individuals with genetic variants, while secondary outcomes showed no significant associations. Conclusions: Pathogenic sequence variants and CNVs were associated with numerically higher risks of adverse cardiovascular outcomes in ACHD, but independent prognostic significance was not established after adjustment for multiple testing.

papers.title: Risk-benefit assessment of oral anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation using virtual clinical trials
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) reduces stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), and screening can enable earlier AF detection and OAC initiation. However, the population-level trade-off between stroke prevention and OAC-related major bleeding for different types of AF and OAC therapy remains uncertain, and large randomized trials to resolve this are costly and time-consuming. Methods: A state-transition Markov-like model was developed to: 1) simulate the lifetime course of AF, stroke, major bleeding, and death in different virtual populations; 2) quantify benefits (stroke reduction) and harms (major bleeding) of systematic AF screening with screening-triggered OAC across CHA2DS2-VA scores; and 3) compare rhythm-guided, time-delimited ("pill-in-pocket") OAC with continuous OAC. Results: The model synthesized information from multiple clinical sources and reproduced stroke and bleeding incidence across clinical scenarios. At CHA?DS?-VA=2, long-term continuous rhythm monitoring (LT-CRM) with OAC lowered stroke risk (HR, 0.92 [95%CI, 0.88-0.96]) but raised bleeding risk (HR, 1.17 [95%CI, 1.07-1.27]) versus no screening. Time-to-benefit was shorter than time-to-harm for CHA?DS?-VA?4, but longer for CHA?DS?-VA=0. Pill-in-pocket OAC vs continuous OAC showed no difference in stroke/mortality (HR, 1.03, 95%CI [0.91-1.16]) but lower bleeding risk (HR, 0.81, 95%CI: 0.68-0.96]) in patients with elevated bleeding risk, but not at baseline. Sensitivity analyses revealed that the risk-benefit profiles of screening or pill-in-pocket OAC strategy further depend on OAC adherence and bleeding risks. Conclusions: Our model highlights a trade-off between stroke reduction and bleeding for systematic screening-initiated OAC, with net benefit for CHA?DS?-VA?4. We provide the first virtual implementation of an ongoing rhythm-guided OAC trial, showing that pill-in-pocket OAC may lower bleeding risk compared to continuous OAC, highlighting the potential of virtual clinical trials to guide clinical trial design.

papers.title: Uncovering Distinct Phenotypes of Early Onset Heart Failure in Women
papers.abstract: Background: Heart failure in younger women is understudied and may reflect heterogeneous pathways and risk not adequately captured by conventional classifications. We aimed to identify clinically distinct phenotypes of early-onset heart failure in women, assess their prognostic significance, and evaluate their transportability in an independent national cohort. Methods: We identified women aged 18-55 years with heart failure using electronic health record data from a large multi-hospital system. A variational deep embedding model incorporating 283 clinical features was used for unsupervised phenotyping. Associations with subsequent inpatient hospitalization, emergency department utilization, and mortality were evaluated using age-stratified Cox models. Phenotype transportability was assessed by both applying the institutionally trained model and by independent de novo clustering as a replication analysis in the All of Us cohort. Results: Among 1,407 young women with heart failure (median age, 45 years), four phenotypes were identified: hypertensive pregnancy (n=494), cardiorenal (n=276), autoimmune (n=394), and cardiometabolic-ischemic (n=243), with a bootstrap adjusted Rand index of 0.65 and silhouette score of 0.45. Compared with the hypertensive pregnancy phenotype, risks of inpatient hospitalization were highest for the cardiorenal (HR 2.86 [95% CI, 2.35?3.49]) and autoimmune (HR 2.25 [95% CI, 1.87?2.70]) phenotypes; mortality risks were similarly elevated (HR 4.65 [95% CI, 3.17?6.82] and HR 4.38 [95% CI, 3.03?6.31], respectively) in these two groups. In All of Us participants (n=682), transferred phenotypes retained their principal clinical characteristics and continued to stratify hospitalization risk. Independent clustering most strongly reproduced the cardiorenal phenotype (Jaccard index, 0.744). Conclusions: Early-onset heart failure in women comprises distinct cardio-obstetric, cardiorenal, autoimmune, and cardiometabolic-ischemic phenotypes with divergent clinical outcomes. These findings support a life-course approach to heart failure classification in women that complements conventional frameworks and incorporates pregnancy history and female-predominant systemic conditions.

papers.title: Waist-to-Height Ratio Identifies Cardiometabolic Risk Not Captured by Body Mass Index: The All of Us Research Program
papers.abstract: Background: Body mass index (BMI) does not characterize central adiposity and may obscure cardiometabolic risk among adults classified as normal weight. We evaluated associations between waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) and incident disease across the BMI spectrum and among adults with normal BMI. Methods: We studied 308,600 adults in the All of Us Research Program. Participants with the corresponding prevalent disease were excluded separately for eight cardiometabolic outcomes. Cause-specific Cox models adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, smoking, and BMI-related factors. We evaluated continuous and nonlinear WHtR associations, elevated WHtR among normal-BMI adults, and incremental discrimination. Additional analyses tested WHtR-by-BMI-category interactions. Results: Among 77,684 adults with normal BMI, 24,301 (31.3%) had WHtR 0.50. In whole-cohort analyses, adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) per 0.05 higher WHtR ranged from 1.07 to 1.31 across the eight outcomes. In BMI-stratified interaction models, corresponding diabetes HRs were 1.52 (95% CI, 1.43-1.61) in normal BMI, 1.42 (1.36-1.49) in overweight, and 1.22 (1.20-1.25) in obesity (P for interaction <0.001). Hypertension associations also differed across BMI groups (P for interaction <0.001). Among normal-BMI adults, WHtR 0.50 versus <0.50 was associated with diabetes (HR, 1.74), myocardial infarction (1.49), and ischemic stroke (1.52). Associations with all eight outcomes persisted in normal-BMI landmark analyses excluding the first year. Flexible age adjustment preserved the principal findings. Adding nonlinear WHtR improved cross-validated discrimination, most notably for diabetes (C-index=0.0134). Conclusions: WHtR identified cardiometabolic risk beyond BMI classification. Associations with diabetes and hypertension were particularly pronounced among normal-BMI adults, supporting assessment of central adiposity alongside BMI.

papers.title: Overall Outlook on Life and Cardiovascular Health Behaviors among Adolescent and Young Adult Females: A Cross-sectional Study
papers.abstract: Background: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death among women, with risk factors commonly emerging during adolescence. Emerging evidence indicates that psychological factors, such as optimism, affect cardiovascular health, yet this remains understudied among young women. To assess the association between overall outlook on life and preventive cardiovascular health behaviors among young women. Methods: We conducted a secondary analysis of a cohort of 331 young women aged 15 to 24 years who completed the modified American Heart Association Women?s Health Survey (2017-2018), using multivariate regression adjusted for confounding. Results: Over 50% of young women felt their outlook on life may impact their likelihood of developing a serious illness such as heart disease. Outlook on life was associated with prioritizing and taking care of health (?=0.18-0.19, 95% Confidence Interval (CI) [0.09, 0.29]; P=0.002) and usually following recommended healthy eating (?=0.12, 95% CI [0.03, 0.23]; P=0.016). Young women who identified as black (27.5%; N=91) felt that their outlook on life had a lower impact on their likelihood of developing a serious illness such as heart disease (Odds Ratio (OR)=0.80; 95% CI [0.65, 0.98]; P = 0.04), compared to other racial groups. Conclusion: Our findings support previous observations indicating a cardioprotective role of optimism in cardiovascular health. However, this association may not hold among young women of color, potentially reflecting constraints in their lived environment that limit how much a positive outlook translates into perceived control over health outcomes. Strategies to reduce cardiovascular disease in women should address young women?s cardiovascular health and psychological and contextual factors, with particular attention to young women of color.

papers.title: Door-to-Valve Time and Clinical Outcomes in Acute Decompensated Severe Aortic Stenosis: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
papers.abstract: Background: Acute decompensated aortic stenosis (ADAS) carries high mortality, but the optimal timing of valve intervention is unknown. Objective: To assess the association between time to valve intervention (transcatheter aortic valve replacement [TAVR] or balloon aortic valvuloplasty [BAV]) and clinical outcomes in ADAS. Methods: Embase, Ovid MEDLINE and CENTRAL were searched to May 15, 2026. Hazard ratios (HRs) for delayed versus earlier intervention were pooled using random-effects models with modified Hartung-Knapp inference. Unadjusted short-term mortality risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using the Mantel-Haenszel method. Results: Eight observational cohort studies (n=6,044) met inclusion criteria: six TAVR (n= 5,986) and two BAV (n=58) studies. Patients were approximately 79 years old, and 63% were male. Early-intervention thresholds ranged from <24-48 hours (BAV) to ?22 days (TAVR) from admission. Delayed intervention was not significantly associated with long-term all-cause mortality (HR 1.52, 95% CI 0.46-5.00; p=0.269; I2=58.2%) or mortality per five-day delay (HR 1.09, 95% CI 0.34-3.43; p=0.530; I2=86.7%). Crude short-term mortality was higher with delayed intervention (RR 4.96, 95% CI 1.17-20.92; p=0.029; I2=0.0%), although this association was not robust to sensitivity analyses. Most studies were at serious risk of bias, with substantial heterogeneity in clinical severity, intervention timing, and treatment modality. Conclusion: Point estimates favour earlier intervention, but current observational data do not establish a mortality benefit for an optimal door-to-valve interval, and existing study designs are biased against early treatment. Prospective and randomized-controlled trials on optimal valve intervention timing following ADAS are needed.

papers.title: Trajectories of Estimated Glucose Disposal Rate and Risk of Cardiovascular Disease: Evidence from Two Prospective Cohorts
papers.abstract: Background Estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) is an accessible surrogate of insulin sensitivity and has been associated with cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. However, whether longitudinal eGDR trajectory patterns convey prognostic information beyond cumulative eGDR exposure remains unclear. We aimed to characterize distinct eGDR trajectories and evaluate their associations with incident CVD in two prospective cohorts. Methods We included 4,823 CVD-free adults aged 45 years or older from the Health and Retirement Study (HRS, n=3,258) and the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA, n=1,565). Latent class mixed models identified four eGDR trajectory classes across three waves. Associations with incident CVD were examined using multivariable Cox models. We further fitted joint models including both trajectory class and cumulative average eGDR to assess their independent contributions. Results: Compared with the persistently high trajectory, the persistently low and declining trajectories were associated with higher CVD risk in both cohorts. In joint models, whereas trajectory class showed residual prognostic signal, particularly in HRS, with directionally consistent but less precise estimates in ELSA. In HRS, adding trajectory class improved model fit beyond cumulative average eGDR alone, whereas adding cumulative average eGDR to the trajectory model did not. Direct pairwise comparisons showed that the declining-then-rising trajectory was associated with lower risk than the declining trajectory in HRS, with directionally similar but imprecise estimates in ELSA. Conclusions: Longitudinal eGDR trajectory patterns may convey prognostic information not fully captured by cumulative average eGDR alone. These findings suggest that the temporal pattern of insulin sensitivity may be clinically relevant in addition to cumulative exposure, while the potentially favorable profile of recovery trajectories warrants cautious interpretation and external replication.

papers.title: Interpretable ECG manifolds link longitudinal electrical phenotypes to heart-failure risk in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
papers.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) produces heterogeneous electrical phenotypes whose continuous organization, longitudinal evolution and clinical relevance remain poorly defined. We developed complementary variational-autoencoder representations to map HCM ECG morphology relative to physiological variation and characterize within-subject change. Using 5,194 normal-reference ECGs and 2,594 longitudinal visits from 650 individuals with HCM, we found that HCM overlapped the physiological manifold but extended towards its periphery, while an HCM-oriented manifold largely reorganized shared electrical modes. Mixed-effects models identified longitudinal drift in selected phenotypic axes. A lateral/frontal QRS-force coordinate remained time-dependent after censoring septal reduction therapy, atrial fibrillation and pacing, and lower values were associated with subsequent heart-failure risk in baseline and time-updated analyses. A time-conditioned change VAE identified four interpretable within-subject modes aligned with longer-term trajectories. Sarcomeric genotype was associated with phenotype position but not trajectory rate.

papers.title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists in diabetic patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction - real world outcomes
papers.abstract: AimsTo evaluate the effectiveness of GLP-1 RAs on clinical outcomes in diabetic patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Methods and resultsIn this retrospective observational cohort study, all adults with diabetes mellitus and HFrEF between 2014 and 2025 were identified. Patients treated with GLP-1 RAs were matched to controls using stratified exact matching. The primary outcome was a composite of heart failure hospitalization or all-cause mortality. Treatment effects were estimated using nonparametric bootstrap resampling (1,000 iterations) to derive risk ratios, NNT estimates, and corresponding 95% confidence intervals. Time-to-event analyses using Cox proportional hazards models were performed as a validation analysis. Among 7,878 patients with HFrEF, 793 (10.1%) patients who initiated GLP-1 RA therapy after HF diagnosis were matched to 1,825 controls. GLP-1 receptor agonist use was associated with a lower risk of heart failure hospitalization or death, with risk ratios of 0.58 (95% CI: 0.42-0.77) at 12 months and 0.72 (95% CI: 0.61-0.85) at 36 months. The combination of high baseline event rates and substantial relative risk reduction translated into remarkably low NNT values in the overall population, with an NNT of 17 (95% CI: 11-33) at 1 year and 13 (95% CI: 8-25) at 3 years. Post hoc subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent effects across clinical subgroups, with no significant heterogeneity observed. ConclusionIn this large real-world cohort of diabetic patients with HFrEF, GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy, in addition to guideline-directed medical therapy, was associated with a lower risk of death or heart failure hospitalization. papers.title: Clinical and Social Determinants of Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy Optimization in Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
papers.abstract: BackgroundHeart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) is associated with high morbidity and mortality. Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for HFrEF has been shown to improve outcomes, with higher GDMT scores at hospital discharge being associated with lower mortality, fewer rehospitalizations and reduced healthcare costs. Yet, disparities in the utilization of GDMT remain. In this study, we examined the effect of various clinical, demographic, and socioeconomic factors on the utilization of GDMT in HFrEF patients referred to Cardiology in a tertiary care safety net hospital, using a standardized GDMT scoring system. MethodsWe conducted a single-center cross-sectional retrospective analysis of patients who had an index HFrEF [≤] 40% diagnosis between January 1, 2024, to December 31, 2024, and who were referred to Cardiology at a tertiary care safety net hospital. Baseline characteristics, laboratory investigations, health care utilization, and GDMT score data were extracted at the ambulatory care visit nearest to 90 days from the index HF diagnosis. GDMT score ranges from 0 to 9 factored in doses of beta-blocker (BB), angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor/angiotensin receptor blocker (ACEi/ARB), mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA), sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i), angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI), isosorbide dinitrate/hydralazine (ISDN/HYD). Multivariable logistic regression was performed to examine associations between low GDMT scores (0-4) nearest to 90 days from new onset HFrEF diagnosis and several clinical, demographic, and socioeconomic variables. ResultsIn 200 patients meeting entry criteria, mean age was 62.7 years, 64.0% were male, 47.5% were classified as white and 42.0% as Black. 39.5% had a low GDTM score (<5). The following were less likely to be associated with low GDMT score: diabetes mellitus (adjusted OR: 0.41, 95%CI=0.18-0.91) and frequent medical appointments (adjusted OR: 0.37, 95% CI=0.25-0.54), while higher serum eGFR was more likely to be associated with low GDMT score (adjusted OR: 1.02, 95%CI=1.00-1.03). There was no significant association between GDMT score and age, sex, race, or payer status. ConclusionIn patients with HFrEF referred to Cardiology in our safety net tertiary care center, higher utilization of GDMT at 90 days was achieved in those who have diabetes mellitus, more frequent medical appointments, or lower serum eGFR. There was no difference in GDMT utilization according to age, sex, race, or payer status predictive of lower GDMT scores. Contrary to findings from previous studies, no significant differences were observed across demographic or payer groups, emphasizing the role of healthcare access and utilization.

papers.title: Distinct Sex-Associated Phenotypes of Sudden Cardiac Arrest Across Clinical, ECG, and Echocardiographic Domains: Replication in Two Communities and Comparison with the Framingham Heart Study
papers.abstract: BackgroundSex differences in sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) incidence and outcomes are well established, but risk stratification underperforms in women. It is important to delineate sex-specific patterns in SCA across clinical, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic domains. MethodsWe studied out-of-hospital SCA cases from the Oregon Sudden Unexpected Death Study (ORSUDS; Portland, 2002-2020; discovery) and Prediction of Sudden Death in Multi-Ethnic Communities (PRESTO; Ventura County, 2015-2024; external replication). Sex differences in 38 comorbidities, 19 ECG and 12 echocardiographic measures were estimated using multivariable-adjusted logistic regression. Female sex was the modeled dependent measure (male as reference). ORSUDS estimates were compared with those in the Framingham Heart Study (FHS), a community-based reference cohort, using FDR-adjusted Cochran Q tests. ResultsAmong 5130 ORSUDS cases, 1715 (33.4%) were women (median age, 70.4 years [IQR, 58.7-81.8]) and 3415 (66.6%) were men (65.6 [55.0-76.8]). Compared with men, women had higher BMI (per 5 kg/m{superscript 2}, 1.11 [1.08-1.15]) and higher odds of thyroid disease (2.56 [2.17-3.13]), asthma (2.33 [1.92-2.86]), mood disorder (2.17 [1.85-2.50]), dementia (1.27 [1.02-1.56]), and left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH, 3.13 [2.44-4.00]). Women also had lower odds of coronary artery disease (0.61 [0.52-0.71]), atrial fibrillation (0.67 [0.56-0.79]), prolonged QTc (0.45 [0.35-0.57]), prolonged PR (0.53 [0.41-0.68]), premature contractions (0.77 [0.60-0.98]), sleep apnea (0.53 [0.43-0.65]), and reduced LVEF (0.40 [0.29-0.54]). Most findings were replicated in PRESTO (n=2719). In contrast, several of these differences were reversed in the community (FHS, n=3539;FDR-significant): prolonged QTc was more common in women, whereas LVH, dementia, heart failure, and higher BMI were more common in men. ConclusionsSex differences among SCA cases were mostly reproducible in SCA cohorts, and distinct from sex-related patterns in the community. These results have implications for development of sex-specific SCA risk assessment and prevention strategies. Clinical PerspectiveO_ST_ABSWhat is new?C_ST_ABSO_LIThis study is the first community-based analysis to comprehensively characterize pre-arrest sex-associated profiles across clinical, ECG, and echocardiographic domains, externally validate them, and compare them with a community reference population. C_LIO_LIWomen with SCA were more strongly associated with non-cardiac comorbidities, LVH, preserved LVEF, and mitral valve abnormalities, whereas male cases were characterized by coronary and peripheral vascular disease, atrial fibrillation, prolonged PR and QTc intervals, premature contractions, and reduced LVEF. C_LIO_LISeveral sex associations, including QTc prolongation, LVH, body mass index, heart failure, and dementia, differed in magnitude or direction from patterns in the community reference population. C_LI What are the clinical implications?O_LIOur findings suggest candidate features for future sex specific risk factor analyses and potential components for sex-specific risk models for SCA. C_LIO_LIClinicians may need to recognize the critical need to extend beyond dependence on just the value of the left ventricular ejection fraction for SCA risk prediction, especially in women. C_LI

papers.title: Global thickness for accurate and precise evaluation of post-intervention remodelling in left ventricular hypertrophy
papers.abstract: Structured abstractO_ST_ABSBackgroundC_ST_ABSCardiovascular interventions may impact both left ventricular mass (LVM) and end-diastolic volume (EDV), but the net effect on wall thickness has been difficult to accurately evaluate. Global average left ventricular end-diastolic wall thickness (GT) relates non-linearly to LVM and EDV. We hypothesized that if GT is independent of EDV in health, then GT will be an ideal measure of post-intervention change in left ventricular hypertrophy. MethodsGT [mm] was calculated using LVM and EDV by cardiovascular magnetic resonance as previously validated. The correlation between GT and EDV was evaluated in healthy volunteers. Change in GT following intervention was evaluated for aortic stenosis undergoing valve replacement, hypertension commencing antihypertensive medications, athletes undergoing forced detraining, and aortic regurgitation undergoing valve replacement. The performance of GT was compared to LVM/EDV. ResultsAmong healthy volunteers (n=4461, mean{+/-}SD age 59{+/-}10 years, 50% female), EDV correlated with LVM/EDV but negligibly with GT (R2>0.16 vs R2 View larger version (55K): org.highwire.dtl.DTLVardef@9a4ba3org.highwire.dtl.DTLVardef@1dbe098org.highwire.dtl.DTLVardef@764838org.highwire.dtl.DTLVardef@17f673b_HPS_FORMAT_FIGEXP M_FIG C_FIG

papers.title: Interferon-activated neutrophils characterize coronary microvascular dysfunction in women with ANOCA
papers.abstract: BackgroundCoronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a common cause of ischemic symptoms in patients with angina and non-obstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA), predominantly women. Neutrophils may contribute to CMD via vascular inflammation and endothelial injury. We therefore investigated neutrophil and coronary endothelial cells in women with ANOCA. MethodsIn this cross-sectional study, we collected blood samples from ANOCA patients (n=123, 84% women) undergoing coronary function testing. Complete blood counts (CELL-DYN, n=123) and neutrophil activation (AQUIOS, n=76) were assessed. Isolated neutrophils were profiled using single-cell RNA-seq (n=11). Guidewire-derived coronary endothelial cells (n=7) isolated during coronary function testing were cultured to passage 2 for bulk RNA-seq. ResultsOf 103 women with ANOCA, 23 (22%) were diagnosed with CMD (CFR<2.5). These women showed higher NT-proBNP than women without CMD (234 [136-416] pg/ml vs. 112 [79-200] pg/ml, p<0.001). Neutrophil counts, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and systemic immune-inflammation index were higher among women with a lower coronary flow reserve (CFR). The proportion of activated neutrophils (CD62Ldim) was inversely associated with CFR at baseline. Single-cell RNA-seq identified four neutrophil clusters, including interferon (IFN)-activated and immature neutrophils. The IFN-activated cluster was expanded in patients with lower CFR and its proportion was inversely associated with surface CD62L expression. Immature neutrophils showed reduced translational and increased inflammatory gene expression in patients with low CFR. Coronary endothelial cells from patients with increased CD62Ldim neutrophils showed higher proliferative/metabolic and lower IFN, complement and coagulation pathway activity. ConclusionReduced CFR in women with ANOCA is associated with neutrophil activation, expansion of an IFN-activated neutrophil population, and altered immature neutrophil transcriptional programs. Neutrophil activation is accompanied by distinct endothelial signatures. These findings implicate neutrophil-endothelial interactions in CMD and identify IFN-associated neutrophil states as targets for mechanistic investigation. Clinical PerspectiveO_ST_ABSWhat is new?C_ST_ABSO_LIThis study provides the first characterization of circulating neutrophils in coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD), identifying an increased proportion of interferon (IFN)-activated neutrophils and an IFN-enriched immature neutrophil phenotype C_LIO_LIReduced neutrophil surface CD62L expression was associated with altered endothelial gene expression and increased endothelial proliferative and metabolic activity, suggesting a potential neutrophil-endothelial interaction in CMD C_LI What are the clinical implications?O_LINeutrophil activation and IFN signaling emerge as candidate pathways for further investigation into the mechanisms underlying CMD and as potential targets for future therapeutic research C_LIO_LIThe association between lower CFR in women and an increased IFN-activated neutrophil population supports further investigation of sex-specific immune mechanisms in CMD. C_LI

papers.title: ECG foundation models share an age-related performance disparity that originates in the data, not the models
papers.abstract: BackgroundElectrocardiogram (ECG) foundation models are proposed for clinical use and promoted as fair, yet such claims are rarely tested with subgroup-stratified evaluation. We measured demographic disparities across four ECG foundation models, tested whether mitigation removes them, and asked whether the dominant disparity originates in the models or in the data and the clinical task. MethodsWe probed frozen embeddings of four architecturally distinct ECG foundation models (ECGFounder, xECG, ECG-FM, DeepECG-SSL) in thirteen cohorts on four continents (5.4 million analysed ECGs, 31 endpoints, six held-out cohorts), stratified by age, sex and race. We examined embedding geometry, tested post-hoc correction, larger labelled training sets, comorbidity exclusion and low-rank fine-tuning, and compared each network with an untrained copy of itself and with logistic regression on classical ECG measurements. FindingsDisparities concentrated on age, not sex or race (median worst-group AUROC gap 0.028 vs 0.004 and 0.016; age exceeded sex in 97% of results) and replicated externally (ED-BWH 30-day MACE AUROC 0.81-0.90 under 40 years, 0.64-0.71 at [≥]75). Age formed a smooth gradient in the embeddings, whereas sex, though most decodable, carried no gap. No remedy closed it (low-rank adaptation: -0.007 to -0.004). Untrained copies (r=0.81, 102 pairs) and classical measurements ({rho}=0.90) reproduced the endpoint-specific gaps, and pretraining raised AUROC (+0.067) without changing them. The largest race effect, higher potassium error in Black patients, vanished at matched true potassium. InterpretationECG foundation models carry an age-structured disparity that replicates externally and survives mitigation. Because untrained networks and a classical model reproduce it, the results indicate that it is inherited from the age structure of the ECG and its labels rather than created by the models, so switching or adapting models will not remove it. Age-stratified reporting, untrained and classical baselines, and age-specific thresholds and recalibration are therefore needed. FundingAustrian Research Promotion Agency (FFG; CARDISENSE project, grant FO999922422). Graphical abstract O_FIG O_LINKSMALLFIG WIDTH=200 HEIGHT=70 SRC="FIGDIR/small/26366943v1_ufig1.gif" ALT="Figure 1"> View larger version (23K): org.highwire.dtl.DTLVardef@a948c2org.highwire.dtl.DTLVardef@1e7d8b1org.highwire.dtl.DTLVardef@437b9aorg.highwire.dtl.DTLVardef@67e5a7_HPS_FORMAT_FIGEXP M_FIG C_FIG Research in contextO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSWe searched PubMed, Google Scholar, and arXiv from database inception to October, 2026, using combinations of the terms "ECG" or "electrocardiogram", "foundation model" or "self-supervised", and "fairness", "bias", "equity", "subgroup", or "demographic", with no language restriction. Open-weight ECG foundation models have proliferated and are increasingly proposed for clinical use, and benchmarks compare them on aggregate accuracy without stratifying by subgroup. The fairness literature documents demographic performance gaps in task-specific ECG classifiers, most often for sex or race on single tasks in single cohorts, and the remedies it proposes act on the model (reweighting, adversarial debiasing, group-robust training, fine-tuning). The one subgroup analysis of ECG foundation models we found covered two models of one family on their own endpoints, stratified by age and sex only. To our knowledge, no study has evaluated several architecturally distinct ECG foundation models along age, sex and race across endpoint families and continents, and none has tested whether a disparity found in a foundation model is also present without any pretraining or without deep learning. Added value of this studyEvaluating four architecturally distinct ECG foundation models across thirteen cohorts on four continents, including six held-out external cohorts, we show that strong average and external discrimination coexists with a disparity that concentrates on age, not sex or race, and that replicates externally. The pattern has a consistent substrate: age is encoded as a smooth gradient in the embeddings, while sex and race, both decodable, carry no comparable gap. The gap is shared across every architecture and pretraining objective, and neither post-hoc correction, larger labelled training sets, exclusion of comorbid ECGs nor low-rank fine-tuning closes it. Two controls explain why: untrained copies of the same networks and a logistic regression on classical ECG measurements reproduce the endpoint-specific age gaps, which indicates that the gap is inherited from the data and the clinical task rather than learned in pretraining. Implications of all the available evidenceFairness evaluation of ECG foundation models should prioritise age and report age-stratified performance as a primary result, because a threshold fixed on the pooled population operates at a worse point for older patients than the headline metric implies. Because the gap persists across architectures, vendors, fine-tuning and even untrained networks, switching models will not resolve it. Evaluations should include an untrained and a classical baseline before attributing a gap to a model, and services deploying these models should use age-specific thresholds and recalibration, or at minimum report and monitor performance by age band.

papers.title: Residual Symptoms and Quality of Life in Female Patients with Hypothyroidism and Cardiovascular Disease
papers.abstract: BackgroundCurrent clinical management of patients with hypothyroidism emphasizes thyroid hormone replacement at doses that normalize serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels. However, biochemical correction does not always translate into symptom resolution or restored health-related quality of life (QoL). We evaluated whether higher TSH levels within the reference range would be associated with worse Thyroid-Related Patient-Reported Outcome (ThyPRO)-39 scores, reflecting greater symptom burden. ObjectiveThe objective of this study was to assess residual symptoms and health-related quality of life in women with normal TSH levels in patients with cardiovascular disease being treated for hypothyroidism. Materials and methodsWe prescreened 96 participants who completed study assessments. Following the TSH obtained at the study visit, 14 participants were excluded due to TSH values falling outside the predefined euthyroid range (0.35-4.94 IU/mL), resulting in a final cohort of 82 women. We also investigated whether comorbidities contributed to symptom burden. ResultsAlthough mean composite scores were numerically higher in the upper TSH quartiles, neither multivariable regression nor ordered trend testing demonstrated a significant association between increasing TSH and overall symptom burden (Jonckheere-Terpstra p = .333). Notably, major depressive disorder (MDD) ({beta}=16.93, 95% CI 8.22-25.65; p<.001) and hypertension (HTN) ({beta}=12.45, 95% CI 2.24-22.66; p=.018) were independently associated with greater Thy-PRO-39 scores. ConclusionsMDD and HTN were independently associated with higher Thy-PRO-39 scores, suggesting that comorbidities may be more strongly related to persistent symptoms than modest variation in TSH within the euthyroid range. Our results suggest that in patients with hypothyroidism and cardiovascular disease, comorbidities may be particularly important when interpreting residual symptoms in biochemically euthyroid patients.

papers.title: Electronic Health Record-Based Machine-Learning for Cardiac Arrhythmia Identification in Adults with High-Risk Chronic Disease: Model Development and Validation Study
papers.abstract: BackgroundCardiac arrhythmias may remain unrecognized in adults with chronic disease. Established risk scores primarily address atrial fibrillation. ObjectiveTo develop and internally evaluate an electronic health record (EHR)-based machine-learning model to identify patients more likely to receive a documented cardiac arrhythmia diagnosis. MethodsWe retrospectively evaluated EHR data (2018-2025) from one healthcare organization among adults with type 2 diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chronic kidney disease, or coronary artery disease. Logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost were compared. XGBoost was selected using internal validation, reduced to 30 features using Shapley additive explanations, and evaluated in a holdout set with data ending one day before the index date. Sensitivity analyses excluded information recorded within 30, 90, or 180 days before the index date. An atrial fibrillation/flutter-specific analysis compared XGBoost with CHARGE-AF and HARMS2-AF. ResultsAmong 30,356 patients, 6,835 (22.5%) had a qualifying arrhythmia diagnosis. In 3,051 holdout patients, XGBoost achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.894 (95% CI 0.879-0.908) and an area under the precision-recall curve of 0.792 (95% CI 0.763-0.822). At a 0.5 threshold, sensitivity was 0.564, specificity 0.971, and precision 0.857. AUROC remained 0.896-0.897 across earlier cutoffs. In the common score-calculable atrial fibrillation/flutter subset (n = 2,436), AUROCs were 0.883 for XGBoost, 0.712 for CHARGE-AF, and 0.554 for HARMS2-AF. ConclusionsXGBoost demonstrated strong internal discrimination for documented arrhythmias. External validation and prospective evaluation are needed to assess generalizability and clinical utility.

papers.title: Twenty-Hour Hypothermic Oxygenated Perfusion Preserves Myocardial Viability and Bioenergetics with No Primary Graft Dysfunction After Porcine Heart Transplantation
papers.abstract: BackgroundHypothermic oxygenated perfusion (HOPE) may extend donor heart preservation beyond conventional storage durations. We evaluated early graft function and myocardial cellular and metabolic integrity following porcine heart transplantation after 20 hours of HOPE. MethodsTen donor hearts underwent various preservation conditions: static cold storage (SCS) for 4 hours (n=2), HOPE for 4 hours (n=3), and HOPE for 20 hours (n=5), followed by heart transplantation (HT) in recipient pigs. Graft function was monitored over 3 hours by serial echocardiography, invasive hemodynamics, optical flow analysis, and vasoactive support scoring; myocardial tissue was analyzed by histopathology, flow cytometry, mitochondrial respirometry, transcriptomics, and proteomics. ResultsEjection fraction, right atrial pressure and systolic blood pressure did not differ between groups, and no graft met criteria for primary graft dysfunction. LV contractility was within normal range with comparable vasoactive support among all groups. Preservation-associated weight gain was greatest after HOPE 20h, and histopathology showed comparable findings with edema present in all cohorts, without fibrosis, thrombosis, or necrosis. Cardiomyocyte viability was preserved across all groups. Maximal oxygen consumption rate was elevated in HOPE 20h versus HOPE 4h and SCS 4h, while basal and non-mitochondrial respiration were similar. Transcriptomics and proteomics revealed limited differences in gene and pathway expression among groups. ConclusionsHOPE preserves donor heart viability, mitochondrial integrity, and ventricular function after 20 hours of preservation, without evidence of primary graft dysfunction, supporting extended preservation for heart transplantation. Edema, recovery of function, and metabolic responses warrant further investigation with longer-term monitoring. papers.title: Incremental value of bilateral ankle-brachial index for ten-year heart and cerebrovascular mortality prediction: an exploratory temporal benchmark in NHANES
papers.abstract: BackgroundAnkle-brachial index (ABI) is associated with systemic vascular disease, but its incremental predictive value depends on the clinical comparator, endpoint and validation design. ObjectiveTo test whether a bilateral ABI feature block improves a nonlaboratory clinical benchmark for ten-year death from diseases of the heart or cerebrovascular disease, and whether a limited nonlinear learner improves the same chronological evaluation. MethodsWe rebuilt public NHANES 1999-2004 examination data linked to the 2019 public-use mortality file. Adults aged at least 40 years with bilateral ABI values in [0.20, 2.50] and ascertainable 120-month status formed a survey-weighted analytic subset. Models were trained on 1999-2002, tuned within development cycles, and evaluated on 2003-2004. Primary models were linear clinical logistic regression, flexible clinical logistic regression, flexible clinical plus ABI regression, and histogram gradient boosting plus ABI. Point estimates used full evaluation weights; conditional intervals used 32-replicate Fay balanced repeated replication with 15 design degrees of freedom. The study was not prospectively registered. ResultsThe corrected cohort contained 6,807 participants (4,617 development; 2,190 temporal evaluation) and 409 primary events, including 139 in evaluation. Evaluation AUROC was 0.834 for flexible clinical regression and 0.834 after ABI addition. The paired ABI increment was -0.0007 (95% CI -0.0047 to 0.0032); the paired Brier difference was 0.0008 (95% CI -0.0003 to 0.0018). Boosting plus ABI had AUROC 0.822; versus regression with the same predictor block, its AUROC difference was -0.0117 (95% CI -0.0379 to 0.0144). Its Brier difference was -0.000661 (95% CI -0.001322 to -7.53e-08); the upper limit was extremely close to zero. Neither primary hypothesis of improvement in both metrics was supported. ConclusionsIn this corrective, exploratory chronological benchmark, bilateral ABI did not improve discrimination or Brier score beyond a matched flexible clinical model. The result does not negate ABI associations, establish equivalence, or support treatment decisions. It supports transparent evaluation of incremental information in a new cohort rather than claims of clinical utility.

papers.title: EIT-based non-invasive measurements correlate with pulmonary arterial pressure in patients
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTo investigate associations between electrocardiogram (ECG)-referenced timing markers derived from electrical impedance tomography (EIT) and invasively measured mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) in patients with cardiovascular disease. ApproachEIT, ECG and pulmonary artery pressure were recorded in seven patients during a protocol combining apnoea and phenylephrine administration. Four waveform landmarks were considered: the maximum, the maxima of the first and second derivatives, and the tangent intersection. Their delays from ECG R waves defined eight markers across the heart and lung regions. Within-patient Pearson and Spearman correlations were calculated against unsmoothed invasive mPAP. Main resultsAcross 56 patient-marker combinations, the mean absolute Spearman coefficient was 0.74. Absolute coefficients reached 0.70 in 40 combinations and 0.80 in 27. Each patient had at least one marker with an absolute coefficient above 0.79. The lung second-derivative timing marker exceeded 0.90 in four patients, more often than any other marker, but showed weaker associations in the remaining three. Associations were positive in 25 combinations and negative in 31. Their strength and direction varied across patients and landmarks. SignificanceThese exploratory findings support studying regional EIT timing as a non-invasive correlate of pulmonary haemodynamics. Validation in independent recordings is required before using these markers to estimate pressure. EIT timing markers are associated with PAP changes in patients; however, there is significant variation between patients.

papers.title: How Short Is Safe? Duration of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Before Aspirin Withdrawal After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Dose-Response Network Meta-Analysis
papers.abstract: BackgroundTrials of P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) withdrew aspirin at fixed times, mostly against 12-month dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT), and categorical syntheses disagree. MethodsBayesian model-based network meta-analysis of randomized trials of aspirin withdrawal with P2Y12 inhibitor continuation, with 12-month myocardial infarction (MI) and major bleeding modeled as functions of DAPT duration (Emax and spline). The prespecified estimand was the shortest duration at which the upper 95% credible limit of the odds ratio (OR) for MI versus 12-month DAPT fell below 1.15. ResultsSixteen trials (17 randomized comparisons, 58,068 patients) contributed 929 MIs and 1,102 major bleeding events. The OR for MI was 1.31 (95% credible interval 0.95-2.09) at 0 days, 1.17 (0.96-1.43) at 30 days, and 1.09 (0.98-1.25) at 90 days. Under every model the point estimate exceeded 1.15 below about 3 weeks and fell below it from about 90 days; a 30-day change-point did not fit better. The credible bound was met at 158 days (Emax) and 282 days (spline). Bleeding decreased with shorter duration (OR 0.40 at 0 days, 0.62 at 90 days). Certainty was low for MI below 90 days and the estimand, moderate for bleeding. ConclusionsShorter DAPT reduced major bleeding, and the ischemic cost of aspirin withdrawal declined with duration; a step at 1 month was not supported. A 15% excess of MI could be excluded from about 5 months (Emax) or 9 months (spline). The curves match duration to each patients ischemic margin. RegistrationURL: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/; Unique identifier: CRD420261480692. What is Known / What the Study AddsO_ST_ABSWhat is KnownC_ST_ABSO_LIRandomized trials have withdrawn aspirin after PCI at protocol-defined times from the index procedure to 6 months while continuing a P2Y12 inhibitor, and guidelines support this transition after 1 to 3 months in selected patients. C_LIO_LIMeta-analyses have compared these trials as duration categories and disagree on how short is safe. C_LI What the Study AddsO_LIWith duration modeled as a continuous exposure, the ischemic cost of aspirin withdrawal declined with the preceding duration of DAPT and a step at 1 month was not supported, while major bleeding decreased continuously with shorter duration. C_LIO_LIUnder every model the point estimate for myocardial infarction exceeded a 15% bound below about 3 weeks and fell below it from about 90 days; the credible bound was met at 5 to 9 months depending on the fitted function. C_LIO_LIHow short is safe depends on the ischemic margin accepted for each patient, which these curves make explicit. C_LI

papers.title: Wearable-derived daily steps and first recorded cardiovascular diagnoses: outpatient and acute care in All of Us
papers.abstract: Wearable-derived daily step counts are associated with cardiovascular health, but associations with the setting of cardiovascular disease (CVD) recording are less clear. We conducted a retrospective landmark cohort study using linked Fitbit, survey, and electronic health record data from the All of Us Research Program. Steps were averaged over the year before baseline. Eligibility required post-baseline sleep coverage and survey completeness, and classifiable pre-baseline smoking and drinking information; former smokers were excluded. After excluding participants with primary or secondary CVD recorded before baseline and 1,470 with either status during the first post-baseline year, outcomes were classified by the first qualifying primary CVD record during years two and three; a single qualifying outpatient record was sufficient. Among 8,292 participants, 5,780 had no recorded CVD, 2,127 had outpatient recording, and 385 had acute-care recording. Multinomial models adjusted for age, sex at birth, smoking, and drinking categories. Each one-standard-deviation increase in step count (3,299 steps/day) was associated with lower odds of outpatient recording versus no recorded CVD (odds ratio 0.786, 95% confidence interval 0.744-0.830), acute-care recording versus no recorded CVD (0.659, 0.586-0.742), and acute-care versus outpatient recording (0.839, 0.742-0.948). Both associations relative to no recorded CVD remained inverse across the tested hypothetical allocations of 455 missing-setting cases, whereas the acute-care-versus-outpatient point estimate approached or crossed the null under some scenarios. Secondary exploratory mediation analyses using a pooled score combining sleep, mental-health, and clinical-burden measures identified indirect associations for both settings versus no recorded CVD, but the between-setting indirect contrast was inconclusive. In this selected cohort, the findings highlight the importance of endpoint definition and recording completeness when interpreting wearable-EHR associations. Author summaryWe asked whether daily steps were related to where cardiovascular disease was subsequently recorded as a primary diagnosis: in outpatient care or in a hospital or emergency department. We linked Fitbit, survey, and electronic health record data from the All of Us Research Program. Our selected cohort met wearable and survey data requirements and had classifiable smoking and drinking information; former smokers were excluded. Participants had no cardiovascular diagnoses recorded before baseline or during the following year. We averaged steps over the year before baseline and assessed recording settings during years two and three. Higher step counts were associated with lower odds of both recording settings relative to no recorded cardiovascular disease. These associations remained inverse across the tested hypothetical allocations of cases with missing settings, but the estimated difference between settings weakened or changed direction under some allocations. A secondary exploratory analysis found statistical indirect associations involving a health-burden score, but the indirect comparison between settings remained inconclusive. The findings apply to this selected cohort, rather than all wearable users, and show why recording context and completeness matter when interpreting wearable-health-record associations. Care settings reflect documentation and care use, not simply disease severity.

papers.title: Incremental Prognostic Value of Regional Myocardial Flow Reserve Beyond Global Flow and Perfusion: REFINE PET
papers.abstract: BackgroundThe incremental prognostic value of regional myocardial flow reserve (MFR) assessed by positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) beyond global MFR remains unclear. We sought to evaluate the prognostic value of regional MFR in the international multicenter REFINE PET registry.
